doc.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012

title: Hank Jones's farm, Dave Chase's barn parties, and the unreleased Swiss recording
summary: Rowe notes Jones lived in Oneonta; Appleyard recalls playing for Dave Chase and the Swiss video recording with Jones and Slam Stewart.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I didn’t know that. You know he lived like an hour south of here.
Yeah. He had a farm, didn’t he?

Yeah, because these people that are coming I hope, tomorrow night, from Chase Design, Dave Chase was a frustrated vibraphone player. And every year for about five years he would get me to hire six or five of the leading jazz players in America. I had every one of them playing in Skaneateles. He had a barn party in his barn. And Hank came and played. And so Dave said, “Well what do you want?” So he said, “I’ve just bought this farm, I’d like to have a horse.” Well David had a lot of polo ponies, you know, he was a polo player. David Chase. He said, “Well I can give you a retired polo pony.” He says “That’d be perfect.” He never picked it up. But he was just one of a kind. We made a record when we were there, we made this record of, well it was a recording done by the Swiss government, you know, video and audio. And it was Hank Jones, Slam Stewart, Jerry Fuller, a wonderful drummer from Canada, and myself. And unfortunately the guy in Switzerland will not release it. I don’t know why, after all these years. This is like 40 years ago. And this chap I’ve been in touch with is writing a book on Slam Stewart. And he knew about this date. And he wrote to this guy and said, “Could you tell me what the tunes were that you played” etc. And are you ever going to release that record. It was a wonderful record. Well how can you go wrong with Slam Stewart and Hank Jones?
